L0-R1: Two stiff A-pose mannequins on a blank beige plane. The 1943 figure is a skin-tight beige bodysuit with a hat. The 1782 coat is a flat red slab with a white strip and a crotch gap. The jagged texture seams at collar and ankles, the barefoot black blob feet, the glitchy eyes, and the lack of any weight or contact shadow all make them read as unfinished game assets.
L0-R2: These are rigid A-pose mannequins. The 1782 coat is flat and unfolded, with a hollow-looking torso and a bare crotch seam. The 1943 uniform looks like a skin-tight onesie with no fabric folds. Hands and feet are crude, the shoes look like rubber boots, the faces are blank or have glitchy eyes, and the neck and cuff seams are jagged. The anatomy is fairly proportionate and the shading is soft, so they read as video-game or doll figures more than literal toys. They still don't read as real people.
L0-R3: These are close-up character models with plausible body proportions and rounded musculature, so they are more human than frame_88. They still look like untextured game avatars. They stand in a rigid A-pose with closed or glitchy eyes, and the clothing has no cloth detail or folds. The 1782 coat is cut like a tunic with a bare red crotch panel. The 1943 outfit is a skin-tight beige bodysuit with no pockets, webbing or boots, and bare toed black shoes. The collar and gaiter fringes are broken geometry. The figures hover over a blank gradient ground.

L0-R1: A crowd of blocky, low-poly peg figures with box torsos, stick legs, and tiny heads. Their identical marching poses look like a tabletop wargame or Lego-style set. They are lit well on a tiled floor with hard shadows, which makes the miniature feel stronger, and the repeated clones add to it. The skirt-cone women and flat colour patches have no cloth detail.
L0-R2: The figures are blocky, low-poly, stick-limbed and identical, with flat painted-on details like the blue X. They march in a rigid grid on a huge empty tiled floor. The scale reads as tabletop miniatures or game pieces. Contact shadows are minimal and the walk poses are stiff and copy-pasted.
L0-R3: The figures are blocky, flat-shaded game pieces. They have box torsos, stick legs, identical faces and a uniform stiff march. The women's dresses are plain cones. Because the figures are so small against the huge tiled floor, the scene reads as a tabletop diorama. The shadows are the only convincing element.
